messages.content:
The failing test `testCircleFitting` in `LevenbergMarquardtOptimizerTest` involves fitting a circle to a set of points using the `LevenbergMarquardtOptimizer`. The test includes calculations of the root mean square (RMS) error and other parameters related to the circle fitting.

The current bug report mentions a discrepancy in the handling of weights in the `AbstractLeastSquares` class, specifically in the `getRMS` method. The bug report points out that the weights are multiplicative in the RMS computation, but in the `getChiSquare` method, they appear at the denominator, leading to an inconsistency.

Upon inspection of the `getRMS` method in `AbstractLeastSquaresOptimizer`, we see that the method calculates the RMS value by summing the squares of weighted residuals and then taking the square root of the result. Each residual is multiplied by its corresponding weight in this calculation.

In contrast, the `getChiSquare` method in the same class calculates the chi-square value by dividing the square of the residuals by the corresponding weight for each observation. This diverges from the treatment of weights in `getRMS`.

To resolve the issue mentioned in the bug report, the weights should also multiply the square of the residual in the computation of the chi-square value in `getChiSquare`. This consistency in handling weights in both calculations will align with the mathematical expectations and improve the coherence of the class.

Therefore, the root cause of the bug is the inconsistent handling of weights in the calculation of RMS and chi-square values in the `AbstractLeastSquaresOptimizer` class.

Next, I will suggest the methods that need to be fixed to address this issue.
The methods that need to be fixed to address the issue are:
```
org.apache.commons.math.optimization.general.AbstractLeastSquaresOptimizer.getChiSquare()
```

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
